label: text
text: "TARANTULA" TO RESCUE.

label: text
text: Canton Soldiers Removed on

label: text
text: West River.

label: text
text: In attempting to enforce the unrecognised right of examining all craft on the West River, a detachment of the Canton Government's inspection Corps met with H.M.S. "Tarrantula" a few days ago, with unexpected results.

label: text
text: This British gunboat was escorting two lighters (tbwed by a steam-launch) from Wuchow to Hong Kong.

label: text
text: At Do-sing the "Tarantula" put on speed and patted company. The inspection Corps has a depot at this port, working from a pair (pontoon) in the river. No effort was made at the time to intercept the lighters for foreible examination.

label: text
text: About 12 miles further down river, an armed launch from the depot caught up with the tow. The cowswain was told to bring his launch and both lighters back to the official pontoon. This, he pointed out, he could not do upstream, ignist the current.

label: text
text: The British Flag.

label: text
text: Accordingly, the Inspection Corps told him to anchor one lighter, being the other up, and then return for the second.

label: text
text: Having given these orders, the armed launch returned to Do-sing. But the "Tarrantula" came up river again and found three armed soldiers in charge of the launch and lighters.

label: text
text: These soldiers were removed, in a motor-launch, to the British gunboat which told the coxswain of the tow to proceed on his journey.

label: text
text: With the three soldiers and their gifts, the "Tarantula" steamed back to the Inspection Corps' pontoon at Do-singe where the officer in charge of the Government depot received back his men and their arms, but not the launch and the two lighters.

label: text
text: It was explained that neither the depot's armed launch nor the three Chinese soldiers had any right to hold up vessels under the British flag.

label: text
text:
Foreigners Asked To Pay.
Lighters and tow-boats controlled by the Standard Oil Co., have been convoyed from Canton upwards by armed launches of the Nationalist Government. This procedure has meant that craft under foreign flags have been "searched" by the Nationalist examiners at Samshui, but very few have submitted to the demand.

label: text
text: Requests by foreign merchants at Canton, to the Government, for Chinese Naval convoys, have brought about comical situations. Officials from the escorts, or from the Canton, Naval Department, have asked applicants if they will supply the necessary bunker coal for a round trip, or pay for the services in a sum practically equivalent to arrears of wages owing to the crew. Such suggestions have, of course, been turned down, but the inference is that if traders want protection they will have to find the funds with which the Canton armed launches can operate.

label: paragraph_title
text: TAI O FIRE.

label: text
text: AN OLD MAN LOSES HIS FORTUNE.

label: text
text: OVER 300 PIGS KILLED.

label: text
text: Official figures of the big fire at Ta' O, 'Lantau Island' (in the Colony of Hong Kong) on Thursday evening, are 300 huts gutted and about 50 or 60 saved, 1,200 people homeless and damage at approximately $30,000.

label: text
text: Damage was confined to the several rows of matshed homes, built on stone piles in a series of creeks facing the main street on

label: text
text: the fire occurred) by a stretch of water 100 yards wide.

label: text
text: About 7 p.m. the alarm was raised. Owing to the combustible nature of the huts, the blaze soon spread to adjoining creeks and finally only one row was saved.

label: text
text: Police and other volunteers wud: in mud waste deep to check the ames.

label: text
text:
Thought Pirates Had Come!
As Tal O is about three hours from Hong Kong, No. 3 fire float (the biggest in the Colony) did not reach the scene until about 9 p.m. when the fire was practically over. The shallow water surrounding the locality also hithered effective work.

label: text
text: An old man who owned one of the huts, on hearing the alarm, thought that pirates had raided the village as happened a few years ago. He forthwith concealed a wad of banknotes—his savings—in a crack. On rushing back to get his money, he suffered slight burns in the face. At present it is not known if he was successful in his quest.

label: text
text: Most of these fisher folk keep a few pigs in their homes. In the darkness and confusion about 200 of these pigs were not liberated in time and they perished in the flames.

label: text
text: In addition to actual loss of property, about 1,200 souls will have to seek temporary accommodation. It costs about $100 to build a home such as those destroyed.

label: text
text: Over 40 years ago, Tai O. village as it then was, was wiped out by a disastrous conflagration.

label: text
text: Some of the present unfortunate victims'still remember the event, which was worse than that of Thursday night.

label: paragraph_title
text: “SUNNING” PIRACY.

label: text
text: Commission of Inquiry Appointed.

label: text
text: TERMS OF REFERENCE.

label: text
text: Hon. Mr. E. R. Halifax to be

label: text
text: The following proclamation appears in the Government Gazette:

label: text
text: By His Excellency Sir Cecil Clementi, Knight Commander of the Most Distinguished Order of Saint Michael and Saint George, Governor and Commander-in-Chief of the Colony of Hong Kong and its Dependencies and Vice-Admiral of the same.

label: text
text: Whereas by the second section of the Commissioners Powers Ordinance, 1886, it is enacted that the Governor in Council shall have power to nominate and appoint Commissioners under the public seal for the purpose of instituting, making, and conducting any inquiry that may be deemed advisable and for reporting thereon.

label: text
text: And whereas the Governor in Council has deemed it advisable that an inquiry should be instituted, made, and conducted as to the circumstances under which the s.s. “Sunning was on November 15, 1926, seized by pirates while on the voyage from Shanghai to Hong Kong; and in particular:—

label: text
text: (a) to inquire how it was possible for the pirates to get on board the steamer with arms in their possession;

label: text
text: (b) to inquire how it was possible for the pirates to seize the ship;

label: text
text: (c) to consider the efficiency of the anti-piracy fittings in the ship and to make recommendations as to alterations and additions if any, that may be deemed necessary in the s.s. "Sunning" or other sea-

label: text
text: going ships; and

label: text
text: d) to consider the supply of armed guards, the number to be carried and their administration.

label: text
text: Now I, Sir Cecil Clementi, Knight Commander of the Most Distinguished Order of Saint Michael and Saint George, Governor and Commander-in-Chief of the Colony of Hong Kong and its Dependencies, and Vice Admiral of the same, with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, hereby appoint: you:—

label: text
text: The Honourable Mr? Edwin

label: text
text: Richard Hamix, C.M.G., C.B.E.,

label: text
text: Lieut.-Commander George Francis Hole, R.N.

label: text
text:
Commander Francis N. Miles,
O.B.E., R.N.

label: text
text: William George Goggins, Esq., Captain Alfred James Holland, to be Commissioners for the purpose of instituting, making, and conducting such inquiry:

label: text
text: And I do also appoint you, the said Mr, Edwin Richard Hallifax, to be Chairman of the said Commissioners:

label: text
text: And I do also appoint Mr. Alexander William George Herder Graham to be Secretary to the said Commissioners:

label: text
text: And, I do further, with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, order and direct that the said Commissioners shall have all the powers, rights, and privileges set out in the third section of the said Ordinance and that the examination of witnesses shall be conducted in private:

label: text
text: And I do further require you, the said Commissioners, to report to me your findings in the matter of the said inquiry and your recommendations at as early a date as possible.

label: text

KOWLOON KNITTING MER.
CHANTS ESTATE.

label: text
text: TO-DAY'S PROCEEDING

label: text
text: A somewhat unusual case concerning the administration of the estate of a local merchant who died intestate was made in the Supreme Court this morning.

label: text
text:
On behalf of Mr. Jehangir Hormusjee Ruttonjee, Mr. H. G. Sheldon applied for the appointment of the former as administrator "and collingenda" in respect of the goods of Chan Kwong Hing, otherwise known as C. K. Hing, late of 272 Portland Street, Kowloon.
In making the application for the granting of letters of administration to Mr. Ruttonjee, Mr. Sheldon said that deceased died on Nov. 13, leaving a widow and two daughters abroad and three children in the Colony. Deceased was a sowing machine importer and carried on business at 272 Portland Street, Kowloon. He was also interested in the Management Sang Knitting Company which was managed by him and other family relatives jointly.

label: text
text: Since the deceased had died, said Mr. Sheldon, the cousins had assumed control of the business. On the premises there was a considerable amount of trade stock, securities and books of accounts which were now in the hands of these relatives. Three of the children of the deceased, aged 17,

label: text
text: 14 and 12, had approached Mr. Ruttonjee, who was an old friend of the family, and had asked him to protect their interests.

label: text
text: Deceased's Widow Away.

label: text
text: The address of the widow of the deceased was unknown, said Mr. Sheldon. She was known to be somewhere in Canada. The two daughters away from the Colony were both in America. Mr. Ruttonjee had cabled to the married daughter, Mrs. Davison, asking her to get into touch with her mother and asking her to come to Hong Kong to take out letters of administration. A reply had been received that the mother was ill.

label: text
text: but that the unmarried daughter would be leaving America and would arrive in Hong Kong on January 1.

label: text
text: The Chief Justice (Sir H. C. Gollan) said that he had no doubt that some powers should be given to Mr. Ruttonjee under the circumstances, but as to the terms of the order he was a little doubtful about any stipulation as to the business. He (His Lordship) could make an order with regard to the collection of the personal property of the deceased and its preservation, but he did not think he could extend those rights to the conduct of the business. The relatives concerned might have a perfectly good case. Mr. Sheldon remarked that the business of C. K. Hing was the deceased's solely. It was only the Man Sang which was a family affair. His Lordship said that this sim

label: text
text: His Lordship said that this simplified matters. He would make an order for a grant "ad collingenda," limited as in an order to be prepared and submitted to him. He did not think that this should include the family concern.

label: paragraph_title
text: IANKOW TROUBLE.

label: text
text: KIUKIANG ANXIETY.

label: text
text: Shanghai, Nov. 27.

label: text
text: A message from Hankow suggests widespread strike possibilities, including servants, washermen, railwaymen, and shop assistants. Orders are being given to foreigners to lay in stocks of supplies.

label: text
text: From Kiukiang it is reported that the latest situation is causing considerable anxiety there. Southern troops are trying to enter the Concession.

label: text
text: A message from Nanking says that 5,000 Fengtien troops have arrived at Pukow, en route for Anking.—Reuter.

label: text
text: [Note: Pukow is the railway station opposite Nanking, capital of Kiangsu province. Anking is further south, on the Yangtze and is capital of Anhui province. Anking appears to the next objective of the Southerners now that they have captured Kukiong.]

label: text
text:
Emergency Regulations
Renewed

label: text
text: FOR THE LAST TIME?

label: paragraph_title
text:
Employers Bar Miners'
Officials.

label: text
text: Rugby, Nov. 26.

label: text
text: The conference of miners' delegates met in London to-day to review the district agreements. Reports were made of the stages which had been reached in the negotiations in the various coal-fields.

label: text
text:
Although the negotiations have, it is understood, practically been completed throughout Scotland, Northumberland and Cumberland, no complete district settlement was put before the delegate conference. Therefore no action was taken.
It was reported that in a number of districts the employers had refused to negotiate with the official representatives of the Miners' Federation and that in some cases they were making individual agreements.

label: text
text: The conference passed a resolution calling the attention of the Government to this action of the employers.

label: text
text:
Emergency Regulations.
"The House of Commons, was today engaged with further renewal of the Emergency Regulations.

label: text
text: " There was something like half a million miners back at work out of a million who were involved in the stoppage. "

label: text
text: If in a few days he could satisfy himself that the condition of affairs was such that he could safely waive any or all of the regulations he would get the necessary order and bring it before the House for immediate sanction.

label: text
text: He added that he was now going to retain the power of prohibiting meetings or processions in his own hands, taking it out of the hands of district Chief Constables. Any prohibition would be made entirely on his own responsibility.

label: text
text: To day's increase in the number of miners at work is 13,083, making a total of 441,571.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: Conference Indignation. London, Nov. 26.

label: text
text: The miners' delegate conference met to review the course of the negotiations in the district settlements, but adjourned without taking definite action, owing to the inconclusiveness of the negotiations up to the present.

label: text
text: The executive will decide further policy after receiving the district reports on the progress of negotiations. A resolution was submitted to the executive unanimously expressing the conference's indignation at the terms offered by the owners in several districts and inviting the Government's attention to the employers' refusal in Notts, Bristol; Leicester and Kent to meet the miners' representatives also in Somerset, until the men had resumed work.

label: text
text: The miners secretary, Mr. Cook, after the meeting, stated that terms had been provisionally reached in Scotland and Lancashire only but had not yet been submitted to "the men.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Three Year Truce

label: text
text:
London, Nov. 26.
Some 441,000 miners were working today.

label: text
text: In Lancashire and Cheshire the coalowners' and miners' representatives accepted the terms of the settlement, including the 8-hour day, continuance of the April rates of pay, and a temporary truce for three years.

label: text
text: A conference of colonators' representatives and miners in Dorbyshire reached an understanding with regard to the terms of agreement.—Reuter.

label: text
text:
Rugby, Nov. 26.
The miners' Delegates Conference meets to-day to consider reports on the district negotiations with the coalowners. In several coalfields, complete agreements have not yet been reached, although settlements are practically completed throughout Scotland, Northumberland and Cumberland. Despite the interference of log, the number of miners working increased yesterday by 7,000, reaching a total of nearly 480,000.—British Wireless Service.
